title: Push safety policy (v1)
description: Server-authoritative policy for the git-push action. Declarative and typed — NOT an embedded rule language. It mirrors the local kernel's reversibility tiers (AUTO/CONFIRM/BLOCK) so the router's own classification becomes an untrusted CLAIM that the verifier re-checks against evidence. The verifier engine interprets ONLY the fixed fields below.

freshnessModes.bound-head: Evidence.boundHead must equal the intent subject head AND producedAt must be within freshnessWindowSeconds of the reference time. This is the server analogue of the kernel's HEAD-keyed evidence freshness.
freshnessModes.window-only: Only the producedAt window is checked (boundHead still must be consistent, but the head-equality freshness rule is relaxed).

notes: The 'push-tier' evidence carries the producer's reversibility classification in claims.tier. The verifier does NOT trust the intent.context.tier field; it reads the tier from verified, hash-checked, fresh evidence and maps it through tierDecisionMap.
If required evidence is missing/stale/forged/contradictory, the decision is BLOCK regardless of the claimed tier (fail-closed).
Absence of a resolvable tier (no valid push-tier evidence) is BLOCK, not ALLOW.
